content_text:
Hi all, a question for everyone and in particular Mr. Deakins.
When on a project, what’s the earliest you’ve gotten an idea for a shot that ended up in the final cut of the film?
Additionally, overall quality of the script aside, have you ever taken a project because a scene in the script suggested the possibility of a striking visual image, or passed on one due to a lack of noticeable opportunity?
I ask primarily because I’ve noticed that in a lot of the more recent Deakins films, I’m thinking late 90’s and onward, there is at least one scene that has a particularly striking visual as a result of the story. An example would be the Oil Fields scene in
Jarhead.
The first time I watched the film, I know despite the phenomenal story, the opportunity to construct those frames alone would’ve temped me to the project.
Thanks!
